title: Sherpa UI View Definition
description: A normalised, id-addressed description of a view: a flat registry of elements plus a layout tree expressed by id references. The App Shell frame (nav / header / body regions) is implicit — a top-level `shell` map assigns element ids to its fixed regions rather than redeclaring sherpa-app-shell. Element `type` is a literal custom-element tag and `props` are literal attribute names — no registry or translation layer. Cross-element wiring is state-mediated: an element `writes` to the `state` blob on an event, and consumers bind their `data`/`props` to it via `$state`. Theme/mode/density are app-level (owned by ThemeManager) and are NOT part of a view.

view.description: Optional human identifier for the view (e.g. 'component-sandbox').

root.description: The id of the element that fills the shell body region. Must be a key in `elements`.

shell.description: Assigns elements to the implicit App Shell frame's fixed regions. The shell itself (sherpa-app-shell) is a given and is never redeclared; you only name which element fills each region. `body` defaults to `root` when omitted.

nav.description: Element for the shell's `nav` slot (typically sherpa-nav).

header.description: Element for the shell's `app-header` slot (typically sherpa-app-header).

body.description: Element for the shell's default (body) slot. Defaults to `root`.

state.description: A free-form state blob. `{ "$state": "/pointer" }` bindings in element props/data resolve against this via JSON Pointer (RFC 6901). An element `writes` to a pointer on an event; consumers bound to that pointer re-populate — no view re-render.

elements.description: Flat registry of every element in the view, keyed by id. Identity is separate from layout: an element is placed by being referenced in a parent's `children` (default slot) or `slots` (named slot), or assigned to a shell region.

elementId.description: Element id — a stable handle for references and state patches.

type.description: The literal custom-element tag to create, e.g. 'sherpa-metric'. Custom elements always contain a hyphen.

props.description: Literal attributes set on the element. Keys are attribute names (data-* for the public API; native attrs like disabled/name/value un-prefixed). Values: string|number → setAttribute(String(v)); true → boolean (empty) attribute; false|null → attribute omitted. A `{ "$state": "/ptr" }` value binds the attribute to state.

data.description: The element's populate() payload. Resolved, then passed to el.populate(). May be an array (1-D collection), a keyed collection object ({rows,columns} / {steps} / …), a precompiled HTML string, a { $state } pointer, or a { src } remote reference (fetched then populated).

oneOf.description: A keyed collection or single record bound by the component.

slots.description: Named-slot fills: a map of slot name → element id (or an array of ids for multi-fill). Slots are regions this element exposes for the parent to fill — distinct from `children`, which is this element's own default-slot content. Slot assignment lives on the parent that owns the slot.

children.description: Ordered ids placed in this element's DEFAULT slot. Named-slot content goes in `slots`, not here.

writes.description: State-mediated wiring. On each listed event, write a value into the `state` blob at a JSON Pointer. Consumers bound to that pointer via `$state` then re-populate — this is how one element affects another (e.g. a quick-filter writes /filter; the grid's data is { $state: /filter }).

on.description: Event name to listen for on this element (e.g. 'quick-filter-change', 'navitemclick').

to.description: JSON Pointer into `state` to write on the event.

value.description: What to write. A '$detail…' path reads from the event's detail (e.g. '$detail' for the whole detail, '$detail.route' for a field). Omit to write the whole detail.

$state.description: JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the view `state` blob, e.g. '/chartData'.

src.description: URL to fetch as JSON, then hand to el.populate(). Equivalent to authoring data-src-json.
